name: Caiaphas
description: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament

points: The rulers of that hour are named, and Annas and Caiaphas are both called high priests. There was to be one, and the naming of two shows how far out of order that priesthood had come.

note.label: Luke 3: The Preaching of John and the Generations Back to Adam

points: And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not. That is Christ, so the whole nation does not die. Because Christ dealt with the whole nation.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

points: On the morrow the rulers, elders, and scribes, with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, and Alexander, and the kindred of the high priest, gathered together at Jerusalem. Annas had been high priest around 6 to 15 AD and kept the title even after the Romans ejected him, while Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was the official high priest the year Christ was killed. These were the very persons who procured the death of Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

cases.name: Caiaphas and the council
cases.charge: Seeking false witness against Christ; condemning him by night; delivering him to the Gentiles; forbidding the apostles; stoning Stephen
cases.preview: The chief priests and Pharisees gathered a council and said that if they let this man alone all would believe on him and the Romans would take away their place and nation, and Caiaphas told them it…
